# Workstation feed assertion reads across different ticks

## Context

PR #20435 head `d0abebaf62705319c871cd84f26ed8e195cda02c` failed [Brain shard 2](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42170234882/job/127736806506) at `WorkstationFeedKeepsScrollNL.spec.mjs:54`: the test expected `feed-00000055` from its sequence read, but the next request returned `feed-00000060`. The scroll assertions passed.

## The Problem

The last assertion awaits `getComponent(storeId, ['sequence'])`, then separately awaits `callMethod(storeId, 'getAt', [0])`. The live producer can add a batch between requests. It compares observations from different ticks even when the newest record is correctly first.

A real Chromium/Neural Link probe on 2026-11-06 forced one existing `Feed#appendBatch(5)` between the old reads: sequence `25`, newest `feed-00000030`. One subsequent `getComponent(storeId, ['sequence', 'items.0.id'])` returned the matching pair `30` / `feed-00000030`. The producer remained live. This is a test observation defect, not evidence of lost ordering.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/workstation/store/Feed.mjs#appendBatch` synchronously adds/trims records, then publishes `sequence` and `batchCount`; its cadence is 500 ms and batch size is five.
- `src/ai/client/InstanceService.mjs#getInstanceProperties` resolves all requested property paths synchronously in one App-worker turn.
- `src/collection/Base.mjs#getAt(0)` returns the first item. The same value is available through `items.0.id` in the existing property reader.
- Design authority: the test's own JSDoc says that at the top the newest event is the Store's first record. Grace, the spec author, confirmed that the assertion needs one consistent pair, not a particular batch.

## The Fix

Change only the final observation in `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationFeedKeepsScrollNL.spec.mjs` to fetch `sequence` and `items.0.id` together. Keep the equality assertion and every existing native scroll/tick check.

Prescription checked: the spec owns the observation; the existing synchronous InstanceService reader supplies the needed primitive. No new API or producer change is required. Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The final ordering assertion compares values obtained in one synchronous App-worker property request.
- [ ] Retain the forced-batch discrepancy and coherent-pair receipt; the test does not pause the producer, add a sleep or weaken ordering into a range assertion.
- [ ] Run the complete spec repeatedly with the real Neural Link fixture; all original scroll/tick assertions pass, and the changed spec is exercised in CI.

## Out of Scope

Runtime feed/Store changes, cadence changes, scroll anchoring and other Workstation assertions.

## Avoided Traps

Stopping the timer or polling mismatched observations until they happen to agree would hide the observation boundary. Preserve one coherent snapshot and the original invariant.
